deities: Lord Shiva as Vaikkathappan (about 6-foot black stone lingam in the circular/elliptical sanctum; worshipped at dawn as Dakshinamurthy, at noon as Kiratamurthy and at dusk as Sambasiva)
Pananchikkal Bhagawati (shrine in the outer prakaram)
festivals: Vaikom Ashtami (12-day annual festival in Vrischikam, November-December; the 12th day is Vaikkattu Ashtami; also observed in Kumbham, February-March)
Vadakkupurathu Pattu (12-day Kalamezhuthu Pattu ritual art to appease Goddess Bhadrakali, held once every 12 years)

history.dynasty: Treta Yuga legend (demon Khara of the Ramayana); temple traditionally attributed to Parasurama, founder of Kerala; standing building dates to the 11th century with 15th-century wooden panels and 18th-century murals
history.period: Legendary origins in the Ramayana era; documented structure from the 11th century onward
history.summary: The Vaikom Mahadeva Temple is one of Kerala's oldest and most revered Shiva temples, honoured as the 'Dakshina Kashi' (Kashi of the South) and grouped with the Ettumanoor and Kaduthuruthy Mahadeva temples as a powerful Shiva trio - worshipping all three before Ucha Pooja is believed to fulfil wishes. Legend says the demon Khara of the Ramayana received Shaiva Vidya Upadesha from Malyavan and three lingams from Shiva at Chidambaram; carrying them southward, he set the right-hand lingam down knee-deep in water at Vaikom (entrusting it to the sage Vyaghrapada), the left-hand one at Ettumanoor and the mouth-held one at Kaduthuruthy. Parasurama, an incarnation of Vishnu, is credited with building the temple and appointing its priests. The elliptical sanctum has a copper-plated roof with a golden kalasam; a 317-foot flagstaff rises in the 8-acre courtyard. The temple also made history as the epicentre of the Vaikom Satyagraha (1924), the temple-entry movement against untouchability in which Mahatma Gandhi took part, leading to all Hindus being admitted to Kerala temples regardless of caste. The annual Vaikom Ashtami festival ends with a 2-km night procession from the Udayanapuram Subramanya temple to Vaikom, where Shiva and Subramanya 'meet' before a farewell circumambulation. NOTE: sources conflict on evening hours (5-9 PM vs 4-8 PM) - verify before visiting.

name: Vaikom Mahadeva Temple
town_description: Vaikom is the oldest township in Kottayam district, on the eastern side of Vembanad Lake about 35 km from Kottayam and 18 km from Kumarakom; it is a backwater temple town on the Kottayam-Ernakulam corridor.

travel.airport: Cochin International Airport, about 56 km away.
travel.railway: Ernakulam railway station, about 33 km; Kottayam station is also on the route.
travel.road: Direct buses run from Ernakulam and Kottayam to Vaikom; backwater trips to Vembanad Lake start from Vaikom Boat Jetty and KTDC Jetty.

visitor_information.best_time: November to January, during the Vaikom Ashtami festival; devotees traditionally receive holy ash (vibhuti) prasadam. Men must remove their shirt before entering the nada; women should wear traditional dress.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 4:00 AM to 12:00 noon; evening reported as 5:00-9:00 PM in one source and 4:00-8:00 PM in another - verify before visiting.
